_comment: These views ARE the technician user interface. The single most important one is
'My Allotted PM List' on PM_Machine_Task: it filters to work that is not yet done,
so when a scan flips Task_Status to Completed the row leaves the list by itself.
That is the whole 'auto-updating list' behaviour - no code, no app, just a filter.
* <Today/> is evaluated server side, so a date filter needs no flow to refresh.
* Filtering on an indexed column keeps the view working past 5,000 items.
* RowLimit Paged='TRUE' is what keeps a big list usable on a phone.

Views.Title: My Allotted PM List
Views.Query: <Where><Neq><FieldRef Name='Task_Status' /><Value Type='Text'>Completed</Value></Neq></Where><OrderBy><FieldRef Name='Cell_ID' Ascending='TRUE' /><FieldRef Name='WO_No' Ascending='TRUE' /><FieldRef Name='Machine_ID' Ascending='TRUE' /></OrderBy><GroupBy Collapse='FALSE'><FieldRef Name='Cell_ID' /></GroupBy>
Views.Purpose: The technician's open work. A completed scan removes the row automatically.

Views.Title: Not Scanned Yet
Views.Purpose: Machines in an open work order that nobody has started. The supervisor's chase list.

Views.Title: Machine Hub
Views.Purpose: The QR landing target. Reached with ?FilterField1=Machine_ID&FilterValue1=<id>&FilterType1=Text, which narrows it to the single scanned machine.

Views.Title: Cells Due This Month
Views.Query: <Where><And><Eq><FieldRef Name='Active' /><Value Type='Boolean'>1</Value></Eq><Or><Geq><FieldRef Name='Cum_Std_Hours_Since_PM' /><Value Type='Number'>3600</Value></Geq><Leq><FieldRef Name='Next_PM_Due_Date_Calendar' /><Value Type='DateTime'><Today OffsetDays='30' /></Value></Leq></Or></And></Where><OrderBy><FieldRef Name='Cum_Std_Hours_Since_PM' Ascending='FALSE' /></OrderBy>
Views.Purpose: Cells at or past the 3,600-hour amber warning, or inside 30 days of their calendar backstop. This is the planning meeting's agenda.
Views.Note: 3600 is the amber threshold for a 4,000-hour trigger. If you retune PM_Trigger_Hours on a cell, retune this view's literal to match - CAML cannot divide one column by another.

Views.Title: Overdue PM
Views.Query: <Where><And><Neq><FieldRef Name='WO_Status' /><Value Type='Text'>Completed</Value></Neq><And><Neq><FieldRef Name='WO_Status' /><Value Type='Text'>Cancelled</Value></Neq><Lt><FieldRef Name='Planned_End_Date' /><Value Type='DateTime'><Today /></Value></Lt></And></And></Where><OrderBy><FieldRef Name='Planned_End_Date' Ascending='TRUE' /></OrderBy>
Views.Purpose: Work orders past their committed end date and still open. Oldest first, because the oldest one is the one production has stopped asking about.

Views.Title: Open Work Orders
Views.Purpose: Everything in flight, with a completion bar per cell.

Views.Title: Open Abnormalities
Views.Purpose: Everything found but not yet fixed. High severity sorts to the top because 'High' precedes 'Low' and 'Medium' alphabetically - a useful accident, but check it if you ever rename the choices.

Views.Title: Overdue Abnormalities
Views.Purpose: Past their committed date. Feeds the daily digest.

Views.Title: Pending Spare Approvals
Views.Purpose: The approval queue, oldest first. The gap between approval and issue is where PMs actually stall, so watch the age of the top row.

Views.Title: NOT OK Findings
Views.Purpose: Every finding, newest first. The follow-up column tells you which ones became corrective work.

Views.Title: Stock Below Minimum
Views.Purpose: Sorted lowest stock first, with the below-minimum rows coloured by the view format. CAML cannot compare two columns, so the comparison is done in the formatting layer.

Views.Title: Latest Upload
Views.Purpose: Newest month at the top, so a missing or late upload is visible the moment you open the list.
